body.statement: Can one derive from \(\mathsf H_q\) an explicit algorithm \(A_q\) that halts on every exact \(P_X\) after finitely many rank, reconstructed-minor, and conditional-independence queries; returns exactly \(\mathcal R(P_X)\) on \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cert}}^{(q)}(K,J)\); retains only realizations of \(P_X\); represents every element of the fully specified domain \(\mathcal C_K(P_X)\); and proves termination with the stated lexicographic measure?
body.justification: Identification without a terminating recovery map leaves the local certificate disconnected from exact diagnosis.
body.gap: Gu (2026) requires two pure items per attribute, Kivva et al. (2021) assumes a mixture oracle, and Lee and Gu (2026) give a heuristic estimator rather than a complete population algorithm.
body.consumer: A positive answer is the mathematical specification for a certified polytomous identifiability checker.
